subject: FargoBank RFP: TAM coverage & incident communication questionnaire
messages:
From: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@fargobank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, procurement@fargobank.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: TAM & incident comms details for RFP

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Our procurement and security teams are compiling answers to vendor operational questions and we need some specifics about Redwood's Support / TAM coverage and incident communications for inclusion in the formal RFP response. Key asks below — we'd appreciate a consolidated response and any supporting artifacts (SLA summary, escalation matrix, templates) by EOD 2027-09-14.

Please provide:
- TAM coverage hours (core hours, timezone references), on-call rota details, and typical response/ack times for critical incidents.
- Escalation path for Sev1/Sev2 incidents including contact methods (email, phone, pager) and expected handoffs to engineering.
- Incident communication cadence and channels for production incidents (initial notification, updates, post-incident report delivery).
- Evidence of processes (runbooks, incident templates, SOC 2 report availability or SOC-related statement).
- Any options for dedicated TAMs or premium support add-ons and estimated SLAs for those tiers.

For context: FargoBank is evaluating vendors for core inference services. Data residency and predictable escalation behavior are gating factors for our security and ops teams. Let me know if you want to set a 30-min sync this week to walk through details.

Best,
Sarah Lowe
Senior Procurement Manager
FargoBank

Thanks — I've drafted answers inline in the questionnaire and exported key artifacts. Summary below (let me know if we need to tighten wording for RFP):

TAM coverage (summary):
- Included TAM (standard): Business hours coverage 6am–6pm PT (Mon–Fri); TAM is primary contact for operational/administrative issues and runbook guidance.
- After-hours support: 24/7 engineering on-call for Sev1 incidents; TAM escalates to on-call via pager and escalation dial-in.
- Dedicated TAM option: available as add-on (monthly retainer) with extended hours 24/7 direct paging and guaranteed response SLA.

Escalation path / response times (typical):
- Sev1 (production outage): initial ack within 15–60 minutes; engaged on-call engineer within 1 hour; continuous updates every 30–60 minutes until mitigation.
- Sev2 (service degradation): initial ack within 4 hours; engineering engagement within 4–8 hours depending on impact; status cadence every 2–4 hours.
- Contact methods: email + ticketing (Zendesk/HubSpot), phone bridge, pager for on-call.

Incident communications & artifacts:
- Initial notification: within 1 hour for Sev1 (contents: impact summary, scope, initial mitigation steps).
- Status updates: cadence documented in incident template; final post-incident report (PIR) delivered within 5 business days for Sev1 incidents.
- Runbook access: read-only runbook extracts and playbooks provided to named contacts; full runbooks available under NDA if needed.

Evidence & compliance:
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; we can provide SOC attestations via our secure portal upon receipt of an executed NDA and data request.
- Audit logs & retention: configurable per deployment; hosted customers have 90-day default retention with options for extended retention on dedicated/private deployments.

Attachments included: tampolicy_v1.pdf, incident_comm_templates_v2.docx, redwood_sla_summary.pdf

Notes / open items:
- Ben: please confirm the pricing bullets for Dedicated TAM tiers and the exact SLA numbers to publish in RFP.
- Elliot: check PIR delivery window and whether we want to commit to 3 business days vs 5.

Marissa
Director, Technical Account Management
Redwood Inference
